html:
The White Mountain Apache are a Western Apache people of east-central Arizona, in the forested mountains of the Mogollon Rim. Like other Apache they speak a southern Athabaskan language, brought from the far north by their ancestors before the 1500s.

They farmed corn in the valleys, hunted and gathered, and raided the Spanish and Mexican frontier. In 1870 the US Army built Fort Apache in their country, and many White Mountain men served as army scouts in the Apache Wars, including against the Chiricahua. Their reservation, the Fort Apache Indian Reservation, covers about 1.67 million acres; its largest town is Whiteriver. The tribe runs a ski resort and timber business, and its neighbours to the south are the San Carlos Apache.
